items: Where was the first caliph chosen after the Prophet's passing?
The pulpit of the Prophet's Mosque
The Ansar and Muhajirun gathered at the Saqifah of Banu Sa'idah and pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr.
Who was the first of the Rightly Guided Caliphs?
The Rightly Guided Caliphs were Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali.
What are the wars Abu Bakr fought against those who left Islam and refused zakat called?
They are known as the Ridda wars.
In which battle was the false prophet Musaylimah killed?
Musaylimah was killed at the Battle of Yamamah under Abu Bakr.
What did the death of many Quran memorisers at Yamamah lead to?
Collecting the Quran into one volume
Umar urged Abu Bakr to have the Quran compiled.
About how many years did Abu Bakr rule as caliph?
He ruled about two years and three months.
About how many years did Umar rule as caliph?
Which event was taken as the starting point of the Hijri calendar?
In Umar's time the Hijrah was chosen as the beginning of the Hijri calendar.
What is the first month of the Hijri year?
The Hijri year begins with Muharram.
Which battle under Umar defeated the Sasanians and opened Iraq?
The Battle of Qadisiyyah (636) opened the way to Persia.
Which decisive battle against the Byzantines led to the conquest of Syria?
Yarmuk (636) was decisive in the conquest of the Levant.
Under which caliph was Jerusalem taken peacefully?
Jerusalem surrendered in 638 by agreement with its patriarch.
Amr ibn al-As conquered Egypt under Umar.
Which battle in 642 broke Sasanian resistance and was called 'the Victory of Victories'?
Umar was stabbed during the dawn prayer by Abu Lu'lu'ah.
Which achievement of Uthman standardised the Quran?
Copying the Mushaf and sending it to the main cities
Uthman had standard copies made and sent to the provinces.
Who became caliph after Uthman was killed?
Ali ibn Abi Talib succeeded Uthman.
What was the battle between Ali and the army that included Aisha called?
The Battle of the Camel (656) took place near Basra.
What was the battle between Ali and Mu'awiyah called?
The Battle of Siffin took place in 657.
Ibn Muljam, a Kharijite, struck him as he went to dawn prayer in Kufa.
What is the group that broke away from Ali after the arbitration called?
They rejected arbitration at Siffin and left Ali's army.
Mu'awiyah founded the Umayyad state in 661.
What was the capital of the Umayyads?
At which place was Husayn ibn Ali martyred?
Husayn was martyred at Karbala in 680.
Which caliph built the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem?
Abd al-Malik completed the Dome of the Rock in 691.
Which caliph built the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus?
The Umayyad Mosque was built under Al-Walid I.
Which commander began the conquest of Spain, and a mountain bears his name?
Tariq crossed in 711; Gibraltar comes from 'Jabal Tariq'.
Which commander founded the city of Kairouan in North Africa?
Which Umayyad caliph, known for justice, is called 'the fifth caliph'?
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz was known for justice and simplicity.
The Abbasid state was founded in 750 by as-Saffah.
Which institution in Baghdad was famed for translation and learning?
The House of Wisdom flourished especially under al-Ma'mun.
Which scholar is a founder of algebra and gave his name to the word 'algorithm'?
Which physician wrote 'The Canon of Medicine'?
It was a medical textbook in European universities for centuries.
Which scholar wrote the 'Book of Optics' (Kitab al-Manazir)?
He is regarded as a pioneer of optics.
Who wrote the 'Muqaddimah', the work on history and society?
He analysed how societies rise and fall.
Who wrote 'The Revival of the Religious Sciences' (Ihya' 'Ulum ad-Din)?
Al-Ghazali's Ihya' is a famous work on ethics and spirituality.
Who compiled the hadith collection known as Sahih al-Bukhari?
It is regarded as one of the most reliable hadith collections.
Imam Malik compiled al-Muwatta' in Medina.
How many books make up the 'Six Books' (Kutub as-Sittah) of hadith?
They are the collections of Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.
Who founded the Umayyad state in Andalusia?
Abd ar-Rahman I founded it in 756 after escaping the Abbasids.
What was the capital of the Umayyads in Andalusia?
Which famous palace in Granada was built under the Nasrids?
The Alhambra is a great monument of Andalusia.
In which year did Granada, the last Muslim stronghold in Spain, fall?
Which scholarly centre in Cairo is among the oldest educational institutions in the world?
Al-Azhar was founded under the Fatimids in Cairo.
Which commander recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders?
Saladin took Jerusalem in 1187 after Hattin.
In which battle did Saladin win a decisive victory over the Crusaders?
Hattin (1187) was a great defeat for the Crusader army.
